target.title: fix(code-mode): use Object.hasOwn instead of Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(obj, key)` and `Object.hasOwn(obj, key)` are semantically identical — both check own properties only, skipping inherited prototype keys. The modern `Object.hasOwn` is shorter, more readable, and not susceptible to a custom `hasOwnProperty` property on the target object.

## Changes

- **`src/agents/code-mode.worker.ts`**: Replace `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(baseTools, name)` with `Object.hasOwn(baseTools, name)` in the baseTools deduplication check.
- **`src/agents/code-mode.test.ts`**: Add test verifying that prototype-named tool identifiers (toString, __proto__, constructor, hasOwnProperty) are safely handled without throwing.

## Evidence

- Existing tests pass: `pnpm test src/agents/code-mode.test.ts`
- New test `"rejects prototype-named tool identifiers in baseTools registration"` passes: confirms prototype-named tools do not trigger errors
- Pure mechanical refactor — no behavior change
